subject.title: fix: don't mark exact-size web_fetch responses as truncated (#101837)

question: Should `readResponseText` use an explicit one-read-over-the-byte-cap contract to distinguish exact-size completion from truncation for `web_fetch`?
rationale: A prior same-root PR was closed as not planned without a content-length/overread contract or real failing response; this branch proposes the overread contract but changes bounded-read latency semantics.

options.title: Accept overread after fixes and proof
options.body: Require the empty-chunk fix, exact-cap/overflow/slow-stream proof, and a refreshed branch before considering merge.

options.title: Keep deterministic cap stop
options.body: Close this PR and leave the remaining behavior to the canonical issue until a real failing response or clearer contract appears.

options.title: Limit to content-length evidence
options.body: Suppress exact-cap truncation only when a trustworthy response length proves the body is complete, avoiding extra reads on chunked streams.

recommendation.title: Accept overread after fixes and proof
recommendation.body: Require the empty-chunk fix, exact-cap/overflow/slow-stream proof, and a refreshed branch before considering merge.
